templates.why_chosen: Two labelled sub-figures (a)/(b) share one time-axis convention and bracket-arrow style to define four latency metrics (BCT, SCT, TTFT, TPOT), showing how a two-panel figure can do definitional work rather than just showing structure.
templates.what_to_learn: For a metric-definition figure, draw one shared time axis and mark each interval with a double-headed bracket labelled by its acronym, keeping the two panels' visual grammar (grid squares for done work, light shading for elapsed time) identical.

templates.why_chosen: Clean two-panel timeline pair: batch inference's long BCT bracket spans completed sub-batches while shorter SCT brackets mark each one, against interactive inference's TTFT/TPOT brackets over a single token sequence on the same time axis.
templates.what_to_learn: Use double-headed brackets to name and measure intervals directly on the time axis (BCT spanning the whole batch, SCT per sub-batch, TTFT/TPOT per token) instead of describing durations in prose, and give each contrasting regime its own panel on the same axis style.
